custom_rng.description: A second, entirely separate PRNG exists: new_rand()/new_srand() (VA 0x406984/0x406a04), a floating-point multiplicative-congruential generator whose single state word is the double at global VA 0x4ff108. It is never explicitly seeded via new_srand() (zero call sites) -- its state is seeded only by the two libc rand()-derived writes at 0x40dccf (new_game) and 0x40f63a (init_game), both of which run before gameplay begins and draw from the libc stream's PRE-reseed state (not from Treplay.random_seed).

custom_rng.conclusion: All 18 new_rand() call sites reviewed are cosmetic/UI (particles, sounds, reward triggers, taunt-text selection, blit jitter, menu). None write into Tfloor/Tmap fields. Because new_rand() draws from an entirely separate state word (0x4ff108) rather than libc's internal rand() state, its calls during gameplay -- however timing-dependent -- CANNOT interleave with or perturb add_floor's libc rand() stream.

add_floor.floor_index_source: m->room[31].level (Tfloor.level, offset 0xc of the 24-byte Tfloor struct) -- an internal counter INSIDE the Tmap struct itself, incremented by exactly 1 on every add_floor() call (every code path that returns increments level exactly once first). This means 'floor index k' = number of add_floor() calls issued so far on this Tmap, independent of wall-clock time or frame count.

add_floor.determinism_claim: Given a fixed seed and fixed per-game difficulty settings (floor_shrink/floor_size/etc., which are constant for the whole game, saved once into Treplay at new_game()), floor k is a pure function of (seed, k): the branch structure that decides both the floor's field values AND how many rand() calls are consumed is itself a deterministic function of k (via the self-incrementing room[31].level counter) and the constant difficulty settings -- never of a prior rand() output, never of time/ticks/player state. Verified: no other live (reachable) rand() consumer executes between two add_floor() calls during gameplay (see libc_rng.rand.call_sites: create_post/scroll_star_field/init_star_field are dead code; fldads_get_random_ad only runs at the menu, before/after play(), never during it).

carrier_requirement: Treplay.random_seed (Treplay+0xa4, saved in every .itr header) is the single value a carrier needs to reproduce tower/platform layout bit-for-bit, together with the fixed per-game difficulty fields already stored alongside it in the same header (floor_shrink+0x8c, floor_size+0x90, start_speed+0x94, speed_increase+0x98, gravity+0x9c) which select which branch/table row add_floor uses. No interleaving order needs to be recorded: the only live rand() consumer during gameplay is add_floor itself, and its own call count per floor is itself a deterministic function of the floor index, not of anything external.
